meta.scope:
Post-hoc control for Exp 19B (added after seeing the 19B result; not preregistered).

Question: Bonsai's ternary codes zero ~32.8% of weights in every tensor family, MSE-optimal
ternary zeros 45.7%. How much of Bonsai's lead over MSE-optimal PTQ does the zero
fraction alone explain? Arm "PTQ_third": per group of 128 zero the 42 smallest
magnitudes in the rotated basis (42/128 = 32.8%), sign of the BF16 weight elsewhere,
least-squares FP16 scale. No data, no training. Same format and tensor set as Bonsai;
BF16 embed/lm_head/norm and original BF16 high-precision tensors.

corpus.special_token_note: Qwen tokenizer has add_bos_token=False and bos_token_id=None; rows are raw text windows, matching prior verified Qwen experiments. Position 0 is excluded from calibration means regardless.
corpus.window_layout: raw 512-token windows; positions 1..511 scored; 4 rows/domain = 2044 targets
corpus.calibration_layout: 4 x WikiText-2 TRAIN tail walking backward + 4 x _pydecimal.py walking forward from token 512; all means exclude position 0
corpus.overlap_6gram_note: rows keys use row-local n-grams; flattened keys include cross-window n-grams inside each contiguous eval stream. Every key must be exactly zero before any calibration row is accepted.

ood_chat.selection_note: round-robin gsm8k,mmlu,humaneval preserving frozen source order inside each suite; minimal prefix covering the eval windows
ood_chat.window_layout: first 4 contiguous 512-token windows; positions 1..511 scored (2044 targets); no padding

causality_precheck_stock.method: three same-shape (3,128) streams: reference, exact rerun, row-2 future perturbed; gated diffs are same-slot
